standard.title: Cohesion devices guide readers
standard.description: Understand that the cohesion of texts relies on devices that signal structure and guide readers, such as overviews and initial and concluding paragraphs
standard.prior_knowledge: Students understand how cohesion can be created through intentional repetition and word associations (AC9E6LA04). They have not yet worked at the level of structural cohesion devices — how overviews, topic sentences, and concluding paragraphs function to guide readers through a text's logic.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students understand how cohesion devices including overviews and paragraph structure guide readers.

nodes.label: Cohesion at the paragraph level
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify how topic sentences and paragraph structure guide readers through a text
nodes.minimum_width: In a given text, identify the topic sentence of at least two paragraphs; explain how each signals what the paragraph is about and connects to the text's overall direction
nodes.typical_width: Examine how topic sentences, sentence openers and text connectives work together to create cohesion across paragraphs — how a reader can follow the text's logic by reading the opening of each paragraph
wider: Identify how authors foreshadow how a text will unfold through sentence openers and text connectives — trace the signposting across a whole text
Compare two versions of the same text — one with strong topic sentences, one without — and discuss the difference in readability
nodes.hinge_reason: If students cannot reliably identify topic sentences at the paragraph level, Node 2's whole-text structural logic is inaccessible — recognising how overviews and conclusions function requires first being able to track cohesion at the paragraph level.

response_modes.reason: Topic sentence identification is a precision skill students use repeatedly across their schooling. Students commonly identify any first sentence as a topic sentence, or miss topic sentences that don't appear first. Practice with varied paragraph structures builds reliable recognition.

success_criteria: Identifies the topic sentence in a given paragraph
Explains how the topic sentence signals the paragraph's direction and connects to the text

nodes.label: Structural cohesion devices
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can understand how overviews, initial paragraphs and concluding paragraphs function as cohesion devices that guide readers through the whole text
nodes.minimum_width: Identify the overview or introductory paragraph and the concluding paragraph in a given text; explain what job each does in guiding the reader
nodes.typical_width: Examine how the introduction (overview of what's coming), body paragraphs (developed with topic sentences), and conclusion (synthesis or restatement) work as a cohesive system — and how each part signals its function to the reader
wider: Compare and analyse the structure of media texts such as digital news sites or print media — how do structural devices create cohesion in texts that may not have traditional paragraph structure?
Examine how the absence or disruption of cohesion devices affects readability — what happens when a text omits an overview or has no concluding paragraph?

response_modes.reason: Students commonly understand paragraph-level cohesion but don't extend it to whole-text structural logic. Seeing how overviews and conclusions function across different text types — including non-traditional structures like digital news — helps students understand cohesion as a principle rather than a formula.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Digital news sites and print media offer a rich context for examining non-traditional cohesion structures — advancing students can investigate how structural devices adapt when texts are navigated non-linearly or in fragments.
success_criteria: Identifies the overview/introduction and conclusion in a given text
Explains how each structural device guides the reader
